guideTitle: 6 Best Overbed Tables for King Beds in 2026
metaTitle: Best Overbed Tables for King Beds in 2026
metaDescription: Six rolling overbed tables that stretch to roughly 66 to 87 inches, compared on length range, power ports, casters and tabletop depth for king-size beds.
introParagraphs: A king mattress is about 76 inches wide, so most overbed tables sold for hospital beds or twin beds simply stop short. The tables in this guide are built as cross-bed desks with long frames, and several of them extend to 83 or 87 inches, which gives the legs room to sit outside the bed frame on both sides.

We evaluated each model from its listed specs and from buyer feedback, without claiming hands-on testing. The lineup splits into fixed-length 87 inch tables, telescoping frames that adjust between roughly 55 and 87 inches, and models that add power strips, lights or a tilting board. Listed capacities and tilt ranges differ from brand to brand, so compare them as stated rather than assuming they match.

Measure before you shop. You need the overall width of the bed frame, the height from floor to mattress top, and the clearance under the frame for the feet. A table is a convenience product, not a support aid, so do not lean on it when standing or transferring, and an occupational therapist can advise on setup for a specific person.

products.name: Condemo 87 in King Overbed Table
products.description:
The Condemo is sized specifically for a king bed at 87 inches long, which is the longest listed reach in this group. Its legs have several manual height settings, and the tabletop carries a four-level tilt board so you can lay a book or tablet at an angle instead of flat.

It also builds in two AC outlets and two USB ports, so a phone, a lamp and a laptop can run from one cord back to the wall. The tradeoff is that the length is fixed, so a smaller bed will not suit it, and a fixed 87 inches needs clear floor on both sides of the bed.

In practice you plug the single cord into a wall outlet, set the legs to the height you want, and roll the table into position. At 87 inches it is longer than the VEVOR at up to 87 inches only when that one is fully extended, but the Condemo never needs an extension step, while the TigerDad Heavy Duty trades that fixed span for a telescoping range. Because it ships in several parts, plan a bit of assembly time and check that each leg height setting is locked before loading it.
products.bestFor: King bed owners who want built-in power and a tilting board on a table that is already full length.

cons: Fixed length cannot shrink for a smaller bed

products.name: TigerDad Heavy Duty Overbed Table
products.description:
This TigerDad table is the only pick here that states a capacity, a listed 350 lb, backed by a reinforced metal frame and a 15mm E1-grade MDF panel. The frame telescopes from 55.1 to 82.7 inches, so it spans twin, full, queen and king beds with one purchase.

Its 47.2 by 18.1 inch desktop is large enough for a 17 inch laptop with a mug beside it. The tradeoff is that the maximum length of 82.7 inches is shorter than the Condemo at 87 inches, so on a very wide king frame with a thick headboard rail you should measure the outside edge carefully.

It is a heavier object than a light rolling desk, so moving it into a bedroom takes a firm grip, and listed capacity is a figure for evenly spread weight, not a reason to stack heavy equipment on one end. If you share a room with a smaller bed later, the telescoping frame is the feature that lets you reuse it, which the Condemo and the Aibiju cannot do. For a table that also tilts, look instead at the TigerDad Tilt, which uses a different frame.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a stated weight capacity and a table that adapts across bed sizes.

products.name: Aibiju King Size Overbed Desk
products.description:
The Aibiju is the plainest table in the group: a large MDF desktop on metal legs with manual height adjustment and a wheeled base. It is sold as a king size overbed table, and the listing leans on its roomy work surface for laptop and home office use.

It has no power strip, no light and no tilt board, which keeps the design uncluttered and leaves fewer parts to loosen. The tradeoff is that the listing does not give exact length or capacity figures, so you should confirm the dimensions with the seller before relying on it for a particular bed.

Setup is straightforward, since the legs set to a height and the wheels do the rest. Compared with the Condemo, which adds two AC outlets and two USB ports, the Aibiju relies on a power strip or extension cord you supply, and compared with the OTUTUMUS it lacks a built-in light. If you mainly want a stable, wide surface for a laptop and a notebook, that restraint can be a plus.

products.name: TigerDad Tilt Overbed Table
products.description:
This second TigerDad is a tilting laptop cart that adjusts in both length and height, and the listing names king and queen beds as the fit. The tilting surface lets you angle a laptop or a book, and the same piece can roll to a chair or a sofa as a mobile computer table.

Its casters measure 1.5 inches and include a brake, which keeps it from creeping while you type. The tradeoff is that the listing gives few exact figures for tilt angle, height range or capacity, so it is harder to compare on numbers than the Heavy Duty model.

A long extended frame needs careful loading, because weight placed near one end acts with more leverage than weight near a leg. At 1.5 inches the casters are small, so thick carpet can slow rolling more than on the VEVOR with its four wheels, two of which brake. It suits someone who wants a single table for bed and desk rather than a dedicated overbed unit.
products.bestFor: Anyone who wants one adjustable, tilting table for both the bed and a desk chair.

products.name: OTUTUMUS Overbed Table with Light
products.description:
The OTUTUMUS combines an adjustable height and length frame with a built-in power strip offering two AC outlets, one USB port and one Type-C port. A soft LED light with its own remote control sits on the table, which helps for reading or for finding the surface at night.

The listing says the table suits sitting, lying or standing use, and the length adjusts to match both queen and king sizes. The tradeoff is that the light and electronics add components that need a wall outlet, and the listing does not give a capacity figure.

Setting it up means choosing height and length, plugging in the single cord, and keeping the remote where you can reach it. Among the powered picks, it offers a Type-C port that the Condemo lacks, while the Condemo has the longer fixed span. It is the one to choose when evening reading in bed is the main job.
products.bestFor: Readers and night-time users who want light and a Type-C port on the table itself.

products.name: VEVOR 66-87 in Overbed Table
products.description:
The VEVOR offers a stated length range of 66 to 87 inches and a height range of 35 to 40 inches, which gives it real numbers where several rivals give none. It has four caster wheels, two of which carry brakes, plus a power socket and an anti-slip edge on the tabletop.

The large surface is described as fitting nearly any laptop, and the telescoping frame lets you shorten it for a smaller bed. The tradeoff is that its 5 inch height range is narrow, so a low mattress or a tall one may land outside the best working height.

Only two of the four wheels lock, so park it where the floor is level and the braked wheels sit on the bed side. Against the TigerDad Heavy Duty, which gives a 350 lb capacity but no power, the VEVOR brings a socket but states no capacity. It is a balanced choice if you want a stated length range and a power outlet.

buyingCriteria.explanation: A king mattress is about 76 inches wide, and the table legs need to sit outside the frame rails, so the span must exceed that by several inches. Aim for at least 80 inches of usable length, or a telescoping frame that reaches it. The Condemo at 87 inches and the VEVOR at up to 87 inches clear that bar, while the TigerDad Heavy Duty reaches 82.7 inches. If your frame has wide side rails or a platform edge, measure from outside edge to outside edge before ordering.

A fixed-length table is simple and has fewer joints to loosen, but it only fits one bed width. A telescoping frame can serve a guest room or a future mattress change. The TigerDad Heavy Duty runs 55.1 to 82.7 inches and the VEVOR 66 to 87 inches, while the Condemo stays at 87. Check that the extension locks firmly, because the joint is where wobble starts.

Depth decides what fits beside a laptop. The TigerDad Heavy Duty top is 47.2 by 18.1 inches, which fits a 17 inch laptop with room for a mug. Look for a stated capacity, and note that only the TigerDad Heavy Duty gives one at 350 lb among these six. Treat any capacity as a figure for evenly spread weight, not for leaning on.

The table height needs to clear the mattress surface and still land near your lap or chest. The VEVOR lists 35 to 40 inches, a 5 inch window, which suits a typical mattress but leaves little room if the bed is unusually low or tall. Measure from floor to mattress top and add the thickness of your lap or pillow. Adjustable legs on the Condemo and Aibiju give several manual settings.

Built-in outlets save a tangle of extension cords, but every added port ties the table to a wall. The Condemo gives two AC outlets and two USB ports, the OTUTUMUS adds a Type-C port and an LED light, and the VEVOR carries a power socket. Check that the cord reaches the wall from where the table will sit, and do not route it where you could trip.

Brakes keep the table from creeping when you type or rest a plate on it. The VEVOR has four wheels with two brakes, and the TigerDad Tilt has 1.5 inch casters with a brake. Small wheels roll poorly over thick carpet, so test the floor type you use. Always lock the brakes before loading the surface.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fit for king bed width
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated the listed length of every table against a roughly 76 inch king mattress. The Condemo leads with a fixed 87 inches, the VEVOR reaches up to 87 inches, and the TigerDad Heavy Duty reaches 82.7 inches. Models with no stated length were marked down for that missing number.

howWeEvaluated.title: Stability and frame details
howWeEvaluated.description: Based on product specs and buyer feedback, we looked at frame material, panel thickness and the number of joints. The TigerDad Heavy Duty lists a reinforced metal frame with a 15mm MDF panel and a 350 lb capacity. Fixed-length tables score well here because they have fewer places to loosen.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power and convenience features
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared built-in outlets, USB ports, lights and tilt boards. The OTUTUMUS offers two AC, one USB, one Type-C and an LED light, the Condemo offers two AC and two USB, and the Aibiju offers none. Features only count when the listing states them clearly.

howWeEvaluated.title: Mobility and parking
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked how many wheels, how many brakes and what size the casters are. The VEVOR lists four wheels with two brakes, and the TigerDad Tilt lists 1.5 inch casters with a brake. Small casters and unbraked wheels lowered a pick's score.

howWeEvaluated.title: Specification transparency
howWeEvaluated.description: Several listings leave out capacity, tilt angle or exact length. We rewarded picks that publish real numbers, such as the VEVOR height range of 35 to 40 inches, and noted where buyers must confirm details with the seller. Where figures are missing, we do not guess.

faq.q: How long should an overbed table be for a king bed?
faq.a: A king mattress is about 76 inches wide, and the legs need to stand outside the frame, so aim for at least 80 inches of usable length. The Condemo at 87 inches and the VEVOR up to 87 inches clear that comfortably. The TigerDad Heavy Duty reaches 82.7 inches, which works on slimmer frames. Measure the outside edge of your actual frame before you order.

faq.q: Is a telescoping table less stable than a fixed one?
faq.a: A telescoping frame has a sliding joint, so it depends on that lock holding firmly. A fixed table such as the Condemo has fewer joints to loosen. Neither is automatically better, but a loose extension is the usual source of wobble. Check the lock each time you extend the table.

faq.q: Can I lean on an overbed table to stand up?
faq.a: No. These are surface tables for laptops, books and meals, not support aids, and none of the listings describe them as such. Weight capacity is a figure for evenly spread loads, and leaning or pulling on the table could tip it. Use a proper grab bar or a stable support for standing.

Not always. The Condemo, OTUTUMUS and VEVOR include outlets, while the Aibiju and the TigerDad models do not, so you would use a power strip. Built-in outlets reduce clutter but tie the table to a wall socket, and the cord must not cross a walkway. Pick them if you plug in more than one device.

faq.q: How do I keep the table from rolling away?
faq.a: Lock every brake before you load the surface. The VEVOR has four wheels with two brakes, and the TigerDad Tilt has 1.5 inch casters with a brake. On thick carpet small wheels may drag or sink, so test on your floor. Park it on level ground and keep heavy items near the center.

faq.q: Are the listed capacities safe to rely on?
faq.a: Only the TigerDad Heavy Duty states one, at 350 lb, and the others give no figure. Capacity is a manufacturer number, and real stability depends on how the load is placed and how well the legs are locked. Keep weight near the middle and away from the extended ends. If you are unsure, choose a model with a stated capacity.

faq.q: Will a tilt board make reading easier?
faq.a: A tilt board lets you angle a book or tablet so you do not bend your neck as much, and the Condemo offers four levels. Comfort is individual, and a steep tilt can make items slide. Use the board together with an anti-slip edge or a stand. For a night-time lamp, the OTUTUMUS adds a remote light.
